chunks: Via Sahl ibn Ziyad, Muhammad ibn Isa, al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, and Jarrah al-Mada'ini: Abu Ja'far (AS) said:
Indeed we wear the saffron-dyed garments and the vibrant red-dyed ones.

key_terms.الْمُضَرَّجَاتِ: Garments stained or dyed to a bright red or scarlet color; 'mudarraj' implies a vibrant, saturated coloring
key_terms.الْمُعَصْفَرَاتِ: Garments dyed with 'usfur (safflower/carthamus), producing yellow-orange hues; a common dyestuff in classical Islamic fashion

ai.seo_question: Did Imam al-Baqir permit wearing saffron-dyed or red-colored clothes?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) personally affirmed that he and the Imams wear garments dyed with safflower (mu'asfarat) and those dyed with a vibrant red color (mudharrajat). This hadith is narrated in the chapter on wearing dyed clothes in al-Kafi's book on dress, establishing that such colored garments are permissible for the Imams and, by extension, for believers. The statement uses the first-person plural 'we,' indicating the Imam speaks on behalf of the Ahl al-Bayt as a collective practice.
